task: Fix IterTools\Single::padLeft so it can emit from an arbitrarily long or infinite input after bounded lookahead. It may consume up to max(1, length) elements to determine padding before the first output, but must not request an additional element until the consumer advances. Preserve lazy validation of negative lengths, left padding of short/empty inputs, all original values of longer finite inputs, fill values, and sequential output keys. Stream::padLeft must retain its existing semantics.
design:
Keep Single::padLeft a generator and replace its full-source buffer with a bounded prefix buffer inside the existing source foreach (src/Single.php:1064–1086). Preserve the negative-length check before source iteration, including its exception message. Buffer and count values only until $length is reached; then yield the buffered values immediately and clear the buffer. Yield subsequent source values directly. If the source ends short, yield $length minus its buffered count copies of $fill, followed by the buffered values. For length 0, yield source values directly.

The threshold flush remains inside the source foreach body. The source stays positioned on the threshold element throughout buffered output, including suspension at its last yield; only another consumer advance can request the next source element. Use one source traversal and unkeyed yields throughout. This avoids rewinding one-shot inputs, preserves sequential keys, and retains all source/fill values without coercion or cloning. Initial consumption is bounded by max(1, $length), with auxiliary storage O(max(1, $length)) independent of total source length.

Leave Stream::padLeft's executable wrapper unchanged: it already delegates to Single and returns $this (src/Stream.php:1054–1057). Update padLeft PHPDoc in src/Single.php and src/Stream.php and the Pad Left sections in docs/single-iteration.md and docs/stream.md. Explain bounded lookahead, partial consumption of infinite sources, suspension without additional pulls, and negative-length validation when iteration begins, before touching the source. Preserve the existing finite examples and documentation style.

Add tests/Single/PadLeftStreamingTest.php and tests/Stream/StreamPadLeftStreamingTest.php for changed consumption behavior. Extend tests/Single/PadLeftTest.php and add tests/Stream/StreamPadLeftTest.php for preserved behavior. Retain all existing assertions, including StreamSingleTier3Test. Follow existing strict types, namespaces, TestCase, static providers, @test/@dataProvider, Given/When/Then, and assertSame conventions. Reuse existing fixtures; guarded sources remain inside their test files. No API is added; changed streaming tests remain separate from preserved-behavior files.

C1–C2: parameterize guarded recording sources by lengths 0, 1, 3 and infinite/very-long-finite source kind. Start their permitted pull budget at b=max(1,length). Inspect the first output, repeated suspended observations, all buffered outputs, and two tail outputs. At output index j, require key/value j and total pulls max(b,j+1); increase the guard budget only immediately before an explicit next(). An extra pull throws immediately, including at the lookahead boundary. C3: retain existing four-form cases and add full keyed-result assertions covering empty/short/equal/long inputs, mixed/null values, fills, and object identity. C4: verify construction is inert and negative-length iteration throws before source consumption or aggregate acquisition. C5: independently verify fluent identity, deferred behavior, finite values/keys, manual suspension, and limited infinite-source consumption through Stream.

C6: during implementation, run focused contract commands through dark-factory verify with command files. Establish intended guarded streaming failures before production edits, then pass focused checks after implementation. Finally run the unchanged complete gate through the supplied helper: php -d memory_limit=2G vendor/bin/phpunit --configuration=tests/phpunit.xml tests/Single && php -d memory_limit=2G vendor/bin/phpunit --configuration=tests/phpunit.xml tests/Stream. Inspect recorded cwd, overrides, output, and exit status. C7: review all four documentation locations against implementation boundaries.

Assumptions and risks: the bound counts elements delivered by the supplied iterable; short/empty inputs necessarily require exhaustion detection. Prefetch internal to a supplied iterable is outside padLeft's control. Large requested lengths still require proportional prefix storage. Main risks are an extra threshold pull, duplicated/lost boundary values, reset keys, and eager validation; focused tests target each. No dependencies, verification configuration, project defaults, unrelated APIs, or translations need changes. No AGENTS.md was found in the worktree or ancestor instruction paths. Setup's passing baseline is supplied evidence; no checks run during design.

reviews.label: pair-design-1
reviews.summary: The design satisfies all seven criteria at the planning stage. Repository inspection confirms the control-flow approach, test roots, fixtures, wrapper behavior, and documentation targets. No tests were run, as required for design review.

challenges.wrongImplementation: Yield the initial prefix promptly but continue appending every subsequent source value to a retained buffer. The buffer-invariant inspection rejects the unbounded storage; guarded consumption tests also reject implementations that exhaust the source before yielding.

Advance the source to element length+1 before flushing the prefix. The guard permits only max(1,length) pulls at first output, and per-output consumption assertions also detect premature advancement during buffered output.

Replay buffered values with their original keys, discard null values, or duplicate the threshold value when switching to the tail. Full keyed assertSame comparisons across all four iterable forms reject these changes, including type and identity changes.
Validate negative lengths eagerly or acquire the source iterator before checking the length. Construction assertions and post-exception pull/getIterator counts reject both timing defects.

Have Stream::padLeft return a replacement Stream or materialize its source before delegating. Same-instance assertions reject replacement, while construction, guarded suspension, and limited infinite-source checks reject eager consumption.

Report only focused-test success while weakening existing assertions or changing dependencies to obtain a pass. Diff inspection and recorded verification provenance require preserved checks, unchanged dependencies, and successful execution of both complete scoped suites.

Document immediate negative-length rejection or claim that fully collecting an infinite input terminates. The four-location documentation review explicitly compares these claims with deferred validation, bounded lookahead, and partial-consumption semantics.

criteria.note: The design replaces the full-source buffer in src/Single.php:1064 with a capped prefix and direct tail yields. Lengths 0, 1, and 3 receive guarded infinite and very-long-finite tests; inspection establishes the universal storage bound.

Flushing inside the existing source foreach preserves suspension on the threshold element. The contract checks every buffered output, repeated suspended observations, and two tail outputs with explicit pull budgets.

Existing PadLeftTest covers four iterable forms. Planned keyed comparisons extend this to mixed/null values, object identity, and empty/short/equal/long cases. Inspected fixtures confirm keyed generators and aggregates preserve input keys; native ArrayIterator correctly avoids ArrayIteratorFixture's numeric-index restriction.

Keeping the existing negative-length check inside the generator and before foreach preserves deferred validation. Planned post-exception assertions use recording generators and the existing CountingIteratorAggregateFixture to establish source non-consumption.

src/Stream.php:1054 delegates to Single and returns $this. Stream::getIterator delegates to Transform::toIterator, which returns an existing Generator unchanged. Independent wrapper tests cover identity, validation, keys, suspension, and limited consumption; Single::limit returns before requesting another source element.

tests/phpunit.xml registers Fixture, Single, and Stream at lines 9, 16, and 18 with suffix Test.php; composer.json maps IterTools\Tests\ to tests/. All proposed test roots and fixtures exist. Changed streaming tests have separate files, existing assertions are retained, and the design requires the unchanged full gate through the supplied helper. Execution remains an implementation-stage obligation.

Both padLeft PHPDoc blocks and the existing Pad Left sections in docs/single-iteration.md:799 and docs/stream.md:2114 were inspected. The planned updates preserve finite examples and explicitly cover lookahead, suspension, infinite-source prefixes, and deferred negative-length validation.

reviews.label: pair-code-2
reviews.summary: Reviewed the entire eight-file diff and confirmed the checkout matches the measured snapshot. No actionable defects found. All acceptance criteria are met; the supplied required gate passed.

criteria.note: Single::padLeft caps its count and buffer at length, flushes at the threshold, and streams subsequent values directly. Guarded tests cover lengths 0, 1, and 3 over infinite and very long finite sources. All six base cases fail specifically on excess consumption; all six final cases pass.

The threshold flush occurs inside the source foreach, preventing advancement during buffered yields. Tests inspect repeated suspended observations, every buffered output, and two tail outputs, increasing the permitted pull budget only immediately before next().

Existing assertions remain intact. Added keyed-result tests cover empty, short, equal, and longer inputs across all four iterable forms, including null, mixed values, fill values, and object identity. The preserved-behavior file passes on both base and final: 109 tests, 121 assertions.

Validation remains inside the generator before source traversal, with the original exception message. Tests verify inert construction and post-exception non-consumption for recording generators and aggregate acquisition. The filtered command executes seven tests and passes on both base and final.

Stream's executable wrapper is unchanged. Tests independently verify fluent identity, deferred execution and validation, finite values and keys, suspension, and limited source consumption. Preserved tests pass on both revisions; all 12 streaming cases fail through the intended guard on base and pass on final.

The recorded exact gate passed: Single 3,825 tests/4,780 assertions; Stream 3,852 tests/162,846 assertions. Verified snapshot identity, command, cwd, overrides, and exit 0. Replay commands isolate their named files; exclusions appropriately retain unchanged fixtures and dependencies while excluding production/documentation changes from test overlays. No dependencies, configuration, or existing checks changed. Diff whitespace check passes.

Both PHPDoc blocks and both Markdown sections consistently describe bounded lookahead, incremental infinite-source consumption, suspension, sequential keys, and deferred negative-length validation. Stream documentation preserves fluent semantics, and existing finite examples remain correct.
